chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Zakat al-Fitrah is incumbent upon every people according to what they feed their dependents, whether milk, raisins, or something else.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Zakat al-Fitrah, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What determines the specific food given for Zakat al-Fitrah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to define the *mahiyya* (essence) of Fitrah, grounding the obligation in local custom (*urf*) rather than a fixed commodity. This principle of flexibility ensures the charity remains a meaningful sustenance for the poor, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting religious duties to the economic realities of the community.
